decanter-stocks.note: Read through a search summary, not the full page.

decanter-report.name: Decanter, 2023 Burgundy vintage report
decanter-report.note: Paywalled. Only search summaries were read.

claims.claim: Winter was dry and mild. Frost at the end of March and early April did little harm because it came before budbreak, around 10 April.
claims.note: One source. Inside Burgundy also says frost damage was minimal, though it describes early April as very cold.

claims.claim: Frost damage was minimal in Chablis and further south.
claims.quote: Frost damage though was minimal both in Chablis and further south.

claims.claim: Damp spring weather brought strong mildew pressure into mid-May. A hot, dry spell from about 19 May got the season back on track. Mildew stayed a worry all season.
claims.note: Vinfolio says May and June were drier than normal and June was the hottest and sunniest since 2003. Inside Burgundy describes a damp first half of May. Both agree on mildew pressure.

claims.claim: Flowering in early June was quick and even in warm, dry weather. Chardonnay had some coulure and made long, loose bunches. Pinot noir set a heavy, compact crop.

Hail was local. It touched parts of the Côte de Nuits on 19 June. A bigger storm in mid-July (11 July per Inside Burgundy) hit Rully, Mercurey and a path from St-Aubin to Meursault. One merchant reports a negociant losing about 40% of its Meursault Premiers Crus.
claims.note: The two agree on mid-July hail around Meursault and Rully. The 40% loss is one producer's figure.

claims.claim: July and August were cooler and wetter than average. Heat arrived late: a heatwave from about 17 to 20 August, then a stronger one from 6 September with highs near 40C that sped up ripening.
claims.note: Sources differ by a few days on the August heatwave (17 or 20 August). Only Vinfolio mentions the September heat.

claims.claim: The Côte de Beaune picked first. A few estates started 24 to 28 August, including Puligny and Volnay. Most began 5 to 7 September. Côte de Nuits estates mostly started from 7 to 12 September. Everything was in before the end of September.
The crop was very large. BIVB-cited figures put Burgundy's 2023 output near 1.9 million hectolitres, about 253 million bottles, a record.
claims.note: Secondary source citing the BIVB. A regional government bulletin snippet suggested nearly 2.2 million hl for AOP wine. Scope of the two figures unclear.

claims.claim: Yields were large, especially pinot noir. Green harvesting was close to universal. Most growers picked at the legal maximum of about 45 hl/ha. Bunches were around twice normal weight. Low-yield estates stayed well below that.
claims.note: Inside Burgundy cites one producer at 45-50 hl/ha after discarding about 30% at sorting, which implies much more on the vine.

claims.claim: Whites are more consistent than reds. Alcohol mostly 12.5 to 13.5%. Best wines pair ripe stone fruit and white flowers with citrus, fresh acidity and a salty finish. Mostly easy to drink young and likely less long-lived than 2022. Some lack concentration or balance.
claims.note: Ageing comparison to 2022 is from one source.

claims.claim: Reds are mixed. Alcohol mostly 13 to 14%. Pinot noir handled the big crop less well. The best are elegant and juicy with light tannins, many approachable young. Weaker ones are diluted, under-ripe or cooked. The Côte de Nuits had more successes than the Côte de Beaune, per one source.
claims.note: The Côte de Nuits versus Côte de Beaune comparison comes from Inside Burgundy only.

claims.claim: In the Côte de Beaune, tasters found clear differences between villages and vineyards. The vintage rarely overrode site. Henri Boillot's 2023s were singled out.

Decanter's reviewer reportedly rates Côte d'Or whites and reds well (search summaries gave 4 of 5 for whites and 4 or 4.5 of 5 for reds), with lush, round whites for early drinking and approachable, fruity reds.
claims.note: Paywalled. The ratings were relayed by search summaries that disagree on the red score. Not used on the sheet.

conflicts: Red score from Decanter varies between summaries (4 vs 4.5 of 5). Not used.
Total crop: about 1.9 million hl (BIVB via Decanter) versus nearly 2.2 million hl AOP (regional government bulletin snippet).
August heatwave start given as 17 August or 20 August.
Côte de Nuits is said to have had more red successes than the Côte de Beaune in one source. A second source stresses wet Côte de Nuits and rot risk. Not enough to rank the two.
gaps: BIVB's own 2023 report was not reachable. Figures come through secondary sources.
The Lay Wheeler and Drouhin pages could not be read (403 and PDF).
No Côte d'Or-only yield or red volume figure found.
Little separate detail on Côte de Beaune red hail losses beyond Meursault, Rully and St-Aubin.

sheet.vintage: A very big crop, so quality depended on how hard growers cut yields. The best reds are juicy and easy to drink young.
sheet.vintage_white: Ripe, fresh and mostly ready early. Whites were steadier than reds. The best have stone fruit, citrus and a salty finish.
